gloss: hit or miss, inconsistency in quality

definitions.gloss: hit or miss, inconsistency in quality
definitions.explanation: Variation in quality or outcome where results can be either good or bad. Often used to describe products, restaurants, or services that are unpredictable in quality.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{当|あ}たり{外|はず}れがある。
examples.english: This shop is hit or miss.

examples.japanese: {安|やす}いワインは{当|あ}たり{外|はず}れが{大|おお}きい。
examples.english: Cheap wine varies greatly in quality.

examples.japanese: このブランドは{当|あ}たり{外|はず}れがないから、{安心|あんしん}して{買|か}える。
examples.english: This brand is consistently good, so you can buy with confidence.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly used in the pattern {当|あ}たり{外|はず}れがある (there is inconsistency) or {当|あ}たり{外|はず}れが{大|おお}きい (the variation is large). The negative {当|あ}たり{外|はず}れがない means consistently good — there are no misses.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {当|あ}たり{外|はず}れがある: to be hit or miss
- {当|あ}たり{外|はず}れが{大|おお}きい: to have wide variation in quality
- {当|あ}たり{外|はず}れがない: to be consistently good
- {当|あ}たり{外|はず}れが{激|はげ}しい: to vary wildly in quality
